definition: Textual case-based reasoning (TCBR) is a subtopic of case-based reasoning, in short CBR, a popular area in artificial intelligence.
details: CBR suggests the ways to use past experiences to solve future similar problems, requiring that past experiences be structured in a form similar to attribute-value pairs. This leads to the investigation of textual descriptions for knowledge exploration whose output will be, in turn, used to solve similar problems.

explainer.lead: A subtopic of case-based reasoning that uses textual descriptions of past experiences to solve similar future problems. It matters because much recorded experience exists as text rather than as structured attribute-value pairs.

tiers.eli5: It's solving a new problem by looking up similar problems you've written about before and reusing those answers.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers investigate textual descriptions for knowledge exploration, then use that output to solve similar problems. Pitfall: standard CBR expects past experience structured as attribute-value pairs, so free text has to be handled differently.
tiers.paperLevel: A subtopic of case-based reasoning, which uses past experiences to solve future similar problems and requires those experiences structured similarly to attribute-value pairs; TCBR investigates textual descriptions for knowledge exploration whose output is used to solve similar problems.

explainer.example: A support team's past written incident reports are explored to find cases resembling a new outage, and their recorded fixes inform the response.
